newsitem.title: USA: Senators seek funds to combat smoking during pregnancy.
newsitem.headline: Senators seek funds to combat smoking during pregnancy.

text.p: Two Senators on Thursday introduced a bill to combat smoking among pregnant women and parents of young children who are vulnerable to "second-hand" smoke.

Sen. Christopher Bond, a Missouri Republican, and Sen. Dale Bumpers, an Arkansas Democrat, introduced a bill that seeks $10 million in additional funds for the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and local nonprofit groups to expand public awareness programmes on the risks.

Smoking during pregnancy can cause birth defects, low birthweight, miscarriage, premature delivery and stillbirth. Babies whose mothers smoke, or smoked during pregnancy, are three times more likely to die of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome, studies have shown.
The latest CDC figures show that 14 percent of pregnant women smoke, and among pregnant teens the figure is 17 percent.
"Not everyone has gotten the message," Bond told reporters. "It is not in the interest of their (pregnant women) health or the health of their babies that they continue smoking."
The bill is backed by the March of Dimes, the American Academy of Pediatrics and other health groups.
